question.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,0],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\pi ,0].$ Find $⟨t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We denote

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⟹ & {u}^{′}=1, \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t & ⟹ & v=\int {v}^{′}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for the integration by parts, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =uv{|}_{-\pi }^{0}-{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t){|}_{-\pi }^{0}+{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡0+(-\pi )\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ))+\operatorname{sin}⁡t{|}_{-\pi }^{0} \\  & =\pi +(\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
